canonical_name: QDax -- QDax: Accelerated Quality-Diversity / 'Qdax: A library for quality-diversity and population-based algorithms with hardware acceleration' (Chalumeau, Felix and Lim, Bryan and Boige, Raphael and Allard, Maxime and Grillotti, Luca and Flageat, Manon and Mace, Valentin and Richard, Guillaume and Flajolet, Arthur and Pierrot, Thomas and others; Adaptive & Intelligent Robotics Lab (AIRL), Imperial College London, and InstaDeep; 2022-2025, JMLR 2024)
lineage: README lists the algorithms it implements with their source papers (MAP-Elites, CVT MAP-Elites, PGA-ME, CMA-ME, OMG-MEGA, CMA-MEGA, MOME, MEES, ME-PBT, ME-LS, DCRL-ME, QDPG, AURORA, Dominated Novelty Search; baselines DIAYN, DADS, SMERL, NSGA2, SPEA2, PBT). docs/overview.md: 'QDax has similarities to the simple and commonly found ask/tell interface'. Code comments cite 'Covariance Matrix Adaptation for the Rapid Illumination of Descriptor Space by Fontaine et al.' for CMAImprovementEmitter. Two files derived from Flax ('Copyright 2022 The Flax Authors'). 'QDax was developed and is maintained by the Adaptive & Intelligent Robotics Lab (AIRL) and InstaDeep.' The README does not name a predecessor project it supersedes. || main loop (reader, from the code): MAPElites.update asks the emitter to emit a batch of genotypes (MixingEmitter samples parents uniformly from the repertoire and applies crossover/mutation; CMA emitters sample from an internal CMA-ES), scores them with the scoring_function to get fitnesses and descriptors, then tell() adds them to the repertoire (each descriptor mapped to its nearest centroid, only the batch-max per cell kept and only if it beats the current occupant's fitness) and updates the emitter state, returning the new repertoire, emitter state and metrics as pure JAX values suitable for jax.jit / jax.lax.scan.

entry_points: qdax/core/map_elites.py MAPElites (holds scoring_function, emitter, metrics_function; init/update/scan_update/ask/tell; update = emitter.emit -> scoring_function -> tell which calls repertoire.add and emitter.state_update)

qdax/core/containers/mapelites_repertoire.py MapElitesRepertoire.add (maps descriptors to nearest centroid via get_cells_indices, segment_max per cell, replaces cell only if fitness > current, functional .at[].set update)
qdax/core/containers/mapelites_repertoire.py compute_cvt_centroids / compute_euclidean_centroids (CVT via sklearn KMeans on uniform samples; regular grid centroids)
qdax/core/emitters/standard_emitters.py MixingEmitter.emit (samples parents from repertoire via selector, applies variation_fn crossover to a fraction and mutation_fn to the rest, concatenates)
qdax/core/emitters/mutation_operators.py isoline_variation / polynomial_mutation / polynomial_crossover (genotype variation operators)

qdax/core/emitters/cma_emitter.py CMAEmitter + cma_improvement_emitter.py CMAImprovementEmitter (CMA-ME: emit samples from internal CMA-ES, state_update re-ranks by improvement and updates CMA-ES state)
qdax/core/emitters/pga_me_emitter.py PGAMEEmitter (MultiEmitter combining a QualityPGEmitter (TD3 critic + policy gradient) and a MixingEmitter GA; PGAMEConfig dataclass)
qdax/core/mome.py MOME + qdax/core/containers/mome_repertoire.py MOMERepertoire (multi-objective MAP-Elites; per-cell Pareto front of bounded length pareto_front_max_length)

Smallest shell commands in tree: 'pip install QDax' (README) and 'uv run pytest -vv tests' (docs/installation.md).
example.input: seed=42; init_variables = jax.random.uniform of shape (100, 100) in [0,1] (100-DoF planar arm); batch_size=1024; num_iterations=50; grid_shape=(100,100); descriptor bounds [0,1]; iso_sigma=0.05, line_sigma=0.1
example.output: repertoire.genotypes, repertoire.fitnesses, repertoire.descriptors (arrays ordered by centroid; empty cells have fitness -inf per MapElitesRepertoire.init) plus metrics dict from default_qd_metrics
